title: The year everything went clear
lede: Crystal Pepsi was the largest product in a short-lived wave. For about two years, taking the dye out of something was a way to say it was pure.

blocks.title: A flat market looking for a new category
blocks.body:
Soft drink sales grew 4% to 6% a year in the 1980s. In 1991 they were generally flat, and some large brands declined.[^6] Consumers were moving to sports drinks, teas and “New Age” drinks such as Clearly Canadian, which claimed to be all natural.[^6] The New York Times put the growth of New Age beverages at about 20% a year.[^8]

Colas were about 70% of soft drink sales[^5], so a cola that borrowed the look of sparkling water was a way to bring the new category to the old one. A Pepsi spokesman described it as taking “a traditional carbonated soft drink” and marrying it “with some of the attributes of the so-called ‘New Age’ products.”[^12]
